questions.q: Why does this capstone require exactly one trigger per object, delegating logic to a handler class?
options: Multiple triggers on the same object fire in an order you don't control, and a thin trigger delegating to a plain class is easier to test and read
Salesforce technically forbids more than one trigger per object
Handler classes run faster than trigger bodies
Triggers cannot contain if statements
questions.explain: Multiple triggers on one object can fire in an uncontrolled relative order; the one-trigger-per-object pattern avoids that and keeps the real logic in a testable, readable handler class.

questions.q: What does `Trigger.oldMap` provide that `Trigger.old` does not?
options: Access to records that will be inserted, not yet in the database
Write access to field values during an after trigger
An Id-keyed map of the previous record states, useful for efficient lookup during bulk updates
A list of records sorted by creation date
questions.explain: Trigger.oldMap gives an Id-keyed map of the prior record states, letting you look up a specific record's old values directly instead of looping through Trigger.old to find it.

It permanently deletes the invalid record
It sends an email to the Salesforce admin
It blocks the save for that record and surfaces a user-facing error message, similar to a validation rule
questions.explain: addError() blocks the save for that specific record with a user-facing message, rolling back the operation for that record exactly as a validation rule failure would.

questions.q: Why can't `WarrantyClaimTrigger`'s `afterInsert` call the manufacturer's REST API directly?
options: Apex cannot make HTTP callouts under any circumstances
Apex disallows synchronous callouts from trigger context because the trigger runs inside the same transaction as the DML that fired it, and a callout could hold that transaction open too long
Named Credentials only work in Flow, not Apex
Warranty_Claim__c does not support after-insert logic
questions.explain: A callout can take seconds, and holding the trigger's transaction (and any locks it holds) open that long is disallowed -- which is why the callout is handed off to a separate Queueable job instead.

questions.q: Per the order of execution described in this lesson, what runs immediately after before-triggers and before the database save?
options: After-triggers
Workflow rules
System and custom validation rules, then duplicate rules
Other Flow automation
questions.explain: The order runs before-triggers, then validation rules, then duplicate rules, then the (uncommitted) database save, then after-triggers, then assignment/workflow/Flow, then commit.
